Arrhenius believed that for mol­e­cules to react upon collision they must become “ac­ tivated,” so the parameter Ea came to be known as the ­activation energy. His ideas were refined by later scientists. In 1915 A. Marcelin pointed out that, while mol­e­ cules make many collisions, not all collisions are reactive. Only those collisions for which the collision energy (i.e., the relative translational kinetic energy of the collid­ ing mol­e­cules) exceeds some critical energy result in reaction. Thus, Marcelin gave a dynamic interpretation for the activation energy inferred from reaction rates.
